title: BOD5 Test — 5-Day Biochemical Oxygen Demand
reagents: Dilution water (with nutrient buffer, seed as needed)
steps: Prepare dilution water and, if needed, seed with an appropriate microbial source.
Prepare sample dilutions expected to give a DO depletion of at least 2 mg/L with at least 1 mg/L DO remaining after 5 days.
Measure and record initial DO (D1) for sample bottles and seed blank bottles (B1).
Incubate all bottles at 20°C in the dark for 5 days, sealed with no air bubbles.
After 5 days, measure and record final DO (D2 and B2).
Calculate BOD5 using the BOD5 calculator with D1, D2, B1, B2, seed correction factor, and dilution fraction.
safetyNotes: Handle samples that may contain pathogens with standard lab PPE.

title: COD Test — Closed Reflux Titrimetric Method
steps: Add sample (and a blank using distilled water) to COD digestion vials per kit instructions.
Digest at 150°C for 2 hours in the COD reactor.
Allow vials to cool to room temperature.
Add ferroin indicator to each vial.
Titrate sample and blank with standardized FAS titrant to the color change endpoint (blue-green to reddish-brown).
Calculate COD using the COD calculator with blank and sample titrant volumes, FAS normality, and sample volume.
safetyNotes: Digestion solution contains strong acid and chromium — wear gloves/eye protection and use the reactor's safety shield.

title: MLSS / MLVSS — Gravimetric Method
steps: Pre-dry and weigh a glass fiber filter (tare weight).
Filter a measured volume of well-mixed mixed liquor sample through the filter.
Dry the filter with residue at 103-105°C to constant weight; weigh (filter + dried residue).
For MLVSS: ignite the same filter at 550°C in a muffle furnace, cool in a desiccator, and reweigh (filter + residue after ignition).
Calculate MLSS and MLVSS using the MLSS / MLVSS calculator.
safetyNotes: Use tongs and heat-resistant gloves when handling filters from the oven/furnace; cool in a desiccator before weighing.

title: Settleability / Sludge Volume Index (SVI) Test
steps: Fill a 1-liter graduated cylinder with a well-mixed mixed liquor sample.
Let the sample settle undisturbed for 30 minutes.
Record the settled sludge volume (SSV30) in mL/L.
Measure MLSS on a companion sample (see MLSS/MLVSS procedure).
Calculate SVI using the SVI calculator with SSV30 and MLSS.

title: Dissolved Oxygen — Membrane Electrode Method
equipment: DO meter with membrane electrode probe
reagents: Membrane electrode calibration solution (or water-saturated air calibration)
steps: Calibrate the DO meter per manufacturer instructions (air calibration or a known standard).
Immerse the probe in the sample, maintaining adequate flow/stirring across the membrane per meter requirements.
Allow the reading to stabilize; record DO (mg/L) and temperature.
Use the DO % Saturation calculator with water temperature and barometric pressure correction to evaluate percent saturation.

title: WAS / RAS Sampling Procedure
steps: Identify the correct sampling point for WAS (wasting line) or RAS (return line) per the plant's flow diagram.
Flush the sample tap briefly before collecting, if applicable.
Collect a well-mixed, representative sample in a clean container.
Run required tests promptly (e.g. TSS/VSS, settleability) since activated sludge changes character quickly once collected.
Log sample time, location, and results in the Logbook.
safetyNotes: Treat activated sludge as a biohazard — wear gloves and wash hands after handling.
